subject: surgery
title: Groin hernias: anatomy, Lichtenstein repair and laparoscopic techniques

steps.tx: Groin **hernias** are classified as indirect inguinal, direct inguinal or femoral based on their anatomical relation to the inferior epigastric vessels and inguinal ligament. An indirect hernia passes through the internal deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric artery, surrounded by the spermatic cord coverings. A direct hernia bulges through the floor of Hesselbach triangle medial to the inferior epigastric artery, resulting from transversalis fascia weakness.
steps.say: Groin hernias are classified as indirect inguinal, direct inguinal or femoral based on anatomical relation to the inferior epigastric vessels. An indirect hernia enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric artery within the cord coverings. A direct hernia bulges through Hesselbach triangle medial to the artery due to transversalis fascia weakness.

steps.tx: The **femoral canal** is a small cone-shaped medial compartment of the femoral sheath bounded anteriorly by the inguinal ligament, posteriorly by the pectineal Cooper ligament, medially by the sharp lacunar Gimbernat ligament, and laterally by the femoral vein. Because its boundaries are unyielding fibrous structures, femoral hernias carry a forty percent risk of incarceration and strangulation, mandating urgent elective surgical repair.
steps.say: The femoral canal is the medial compartment of the femoral sheath bounded anteriorly by the inguinal ligament, posteriorly by Cooper ligament, medially by the lacunar ligament, and laterally by the femoral vein. Because these borders are rigid, femoral hernias carry high strangulation risk, requiring prompt operative repair.

vis.alt: Femoral canal box: anterior inguinal ligament, posterior Cooper pectineal ligament, medial sharp lacunar Gimbernat ligament, lateral femoral vein; rigid walls give forty percent incarceration and strangulation risk, mandating urgent elective repair.
vis.caption: Four rigid walls: assume strangulation risk, book the list.

steps.tx: The open **Lichtenstein tension-free repair** is the gold standard for primary inguinal hernia repair. A flat polypropylene mesh is positioned across the floor of the inguinal canal, sutured inferiorly to the shelving edge of the inguinal ligament and pubic tubercle, medially to the conjoint tendon, and slit laterally to accommodate the spermatic cord. Avoiding tissue tension dramatically reduced recurrence rates to below one percent.
steps.say: The open Lichtenstein tension-free repair is the gold standard for primary inguinal hernia repair. A flat polypropylene mesh is positioned over the canal floor, secured to the inguinal ligament and conjoint tendon, and slit laterally around the spermatic cord. Eliminating tissue tension reduced recurrence rates to below one percent.

left.title: Lichtenstein repair
points: Open anterior approach under local anesthesia
Mesh placed superficial to transversalis fascia
Ideal for primary unilateral inguinal hernia
Risk of chronic groin nerve entrapment

right.title: Laparoscopic repair (TAPP / TEP)
points: Mesh placed posterior to myopectineal orifice
Ideal for bilateral or recurrent inguinal hernias
Faster recovery and lower chronic groin pain

steps.tx: Laparoscopic repairs cover the entire myopectineal orifice of Fruchaud from the preperitoneal space. Surgeons must respect two critical anatomical danger zones: the **triangle of doom**, bounded by the vas deferens medially and testicular vessels laterally, containing the external iliac artery and vein; and the **triangle of pain**, lateral to testicular vessels below the iliopubic tract, containing the femoral branch of genitofemoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves.
steps.say: Laparoscopic repairs cover the myopectineal orifice of Fruchaud preperitoneally. Surgeons must avoid two danger zones: the triangle of doom, containing external iliac vessels, and the triangle of pain, containing the lateral femoral cutaneous and genitofemoral nerves. Tacks placed in the triangle of pain cause severe chronic neuralgia.

vis.alt: Laparoscopic preperitoneal view of the groin showing the triangle of doom between the vas deferens and testicular vessels (containing the external iliac artery and vein) and the triangle of pain below the iliopubic tract.
vis.caption: Laparoscopic view of the triangle of doom and triangle of pain in the groin.
